gap: No result ChatGPT got gives BLUETTI's own solar input window for the Apex 300: 12–60 V and 20 A on each of its two XT60 ports, 1,200 W per port and 2,400 W in total, with a 60 V open-circuit voltage cap. BLUETTI therefore tells buyers to wire extra panels in parallel, not in long series strings. No result confirms from BLUETTI that a single Apex 300 gives 120 V and 240 V at the same time, which EnergySage calls unconfirmed and ChatGPT asserted without a source.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, read 2026-11-17) gives the Apex 300 only as 'two native 1,200 W inputs', citing BLUETTI's Apex 200 vs 300 guide, with no voltage or current window. It gives windows for the Jackery HomePower 3000 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra and says nothing on 240 V or expansion batteries. EnergySage (cited) lists the Apex 300 as 120 V/240 V but says it doesn't state whether one unit does it, and notes the unit is AC-only, so DC ports need an add-on hub. Lights On Labs (cited) says the Jackery HomePower 3000 is 120 V only and gives no voltage windows. None of them covers the ALLPOWERS R3500 kits at all. I could not open SolarGenAdvisor: its certificate chain failed in the fetcher.
decides: If the shopper needs 240 V (well pump, dryer, NEMA 14-50 RV), the Apex 300 kits are the ones BLUETTI documents as giving 120 V and 240 V from one unit, unlike ChatGPT's 'best overall' Jackery HomePower 3000 (120 V only per Lights On Labs). But every Apex 300 kit is a pre-order shipping late January 2027, so it is the wait-for option, not the pick. The 60 V cap also means adding panels has to follow BLUETTI's parallel-wiring advice. The R3500 kits ship now, but I could not confirm their US input window, so the page should not claim the R3500 takes the 600 W SP039 at full output.

findings.label: Solar input per port
findings.value: Up to 1,200 W per DC solar port, 12–60 V, 20 A max, two XT60 ports; 2,400 W combined on the base unit
findings.source_title: Building the Ultimate RV Power System in 2026: BLUETTI Apex 300 Full Setup Guide - BLUETTI US
findings.note: BLUETTI's own guide, dated 2026-11-04. Quote: 'accepts up to 1,200 W per DC solar port (12–60 V, 20 A max; two XT60 ports)'.

findings.label: Panel wiring limit stated by the maker
findings.value: Solar input capped at 60 V Voc; BLUETTI says to 'plan parallel panel strings rather than high-voltage series arrays'
findings.source_title: Building the Ultimate RV Power System in 2026: BLUETTI Apex 300 Full Setup Guide - BLUETTI US
findings.note: Exclusion stated by the maker: any string whose open-circuit voltage is above 60 V is out of range.

findings.label: AC voltage from one unit
findings.value: 120 V and 240 V simultaneous output for split-phase rigs (one unit; NEMA 14-50R 120/240 V and TT-30R connections per BLUETTI)
findings.source_title: Building the Ultimate RV Power System in 2026: BLUETTI Apex 300 Full Setup Guide - BLUETTI US
findings.note: The guide's spec table lists '120V and 240V simultaneous output'. The 2×200 W kit page also says it can 'power both 120V and 240V devices simultaneously' but does not say what hardware is needed for a home connection. The 14-50R/TT-30R detail came from a search summary of BLUETTI's Apex 200 vs 300 page, which I did not open.

findings.label: DC / 12 V output
findings.value: No DC ports on the main unit; Hub D1 required for DC power (12 V/50 A or 24 V/25 A Anderson on the Hub D1)
findings.source_title: Building the Ultimate RV Power System in 2026: BLUETTI Apex 300 Full Setup Guide - BLUETTI US
findings.note: The 2×200 W kit's box list on bluettipower.com has no Hub D1, so a kit buyer who wants USB or 12 V must buy it separately. EnergySage (cited) already says the unit is AC-only.
